item.text:
**5B.5 Research Note**
Bottom line: **mixed, leaning positive on anti-rent intent, but with strong evidence that capture-prone structures remained in place and little direct proof of hard anti-graft enforcement against connected actors.**

**Positive**
- [Pakistan: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on Economic Policies with Pakistan for 37-month Extended Fund Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/07/12/pr-24273-pakistan-imf-reaches-agreement-on-economic-policies-for-37-month-eff) — IMF, 2024-07-12. Claim: the new program called for broadening the tax base, improving SOE management, strengthening competition, securing a level playing field, phasing out distortive incentives, and advancing anti-corruption/governance reforms. This is the strongest evidence that Sharif’s government was trying to shrink rent channels rather than protect them. QIDs: `5B.5`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`, `5B.1`.

- [Pakistan: Second and Final Review Under the Stand-By Arrangement](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/05/10/pakistan-second-and-final-review-under-the-stand-by-arrangement-press-release-staff-report-548741) — IMF, 2024-05-10. Claim: the IMF said strong, inclusive growth required SOE reform and stronger governance/anti-corruption institutions. This supports a reformist, anti-capture direction, though it is still program language rather than proof of enforcement. QIDs: `5B.5`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`.

- [Govt unveils broader privatisation plan for state-owned enterprises](https://www.dawn.com/news/1833439) — Reuters via Dawn, 2024-05-14. Claim: Sharif said all SOEs except strategic ones would be privatized and that the state should create a business- and investment-friendly environment. That is direct evidence against state-linked monopolies and patronage. QIDs: `5B.5`, `5B.4`.

- [Govt departments causing ‘billions in losses’ to be shut down: PM Shehbaz](https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1840092) — Dawn, 2024-06-15. Claim: Sharif publicly targeted departments and institutions he described as corruption-prone, promising closures, privatization, and savings of billions. This is the clearest direct anti-corruption rhetoric in the 2024 record. QIDs: `5B.5`, `5B.4`.

- [Pakistan renegotiating power deals to cut costs, minister says](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/pakistan-renegotiating-power-deals-to-cut-costs-minister-says-3606192) — Reuters, 2024-09-07. Claim: the government renegotiated independent power producer contracts to lower tariffs and end unsustainable deals. That can be read as pushing back against entrenched private power rents, though it is not direct proof of anti-graft enforcement. QIDs: `5B.5`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`.

**Negative**
- [Pakistan: 2024 Article IV Consultation and Request for an Extended Arrangement under the Extended Fund Facility](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/10/10/pakistan-2024-article-iv-consultation-and-request-for-an-extended-arrangement-under-the-556152) — IMF, 2024-10-10. Claim: the IMF said weak governance, an outsized state role, a narrow tax base, and a difficult business environment still hindered investment. That is strong evidence that rent-seeking and capture-prone structures were still intact despite reform rhetoric. QIDs: `5B.5`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`.

- [PAKISTAN: Reform Implementation Remains Critical for Continued Economic Recovery and Poverty Reduction, says World Bank](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/10/09/-pakistan-reform-implementation-remains-critical-for-continued-economic-recovery-and-poverty-reduction-says-world-bank) — World Bank, 2024-10-10. Claim: the World Bank said reforms were still needed to the tax system, subsidies, state presence, and trade/investment barriers. This supports the view that structurally privileged access and state distortion were not yet dismantled. QIDs: `5B.5`, `5B.4`, `5B.3`.

**Search gap**
- I did **not** find strong 2024 reporting showing Sharif personally prosecuted a politically connected business figure, reversed a named monopoly benefit, or took a visible anti-elite enforcement step beyond the broad reform program.
- The negative evidence is therefore mostly **structural** rather than case-specific: weak governance, state-heavy markets, and persistent investment distortions.
